subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and if so which scope is allowed: warnings only, structured handoff/checkpoint, bounded deferral, or none?
rationale: The request crosses product UX, public config, persistence, and security boundaries because it can change when agents get extra write opportunities and whether compaction may be delayed after context pressure is detected.

options.title: Warning And Checkpointed Handoff First
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in pre-threshold warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested DEFER disabled until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Full Bounded Deferral Contract
options.body: Allow warning, handoff, and DEFER only with strict max duration, audit trail, idempotent checkpoint matching, scope verification, and approval-expiry rules.

options.title: Keep Existing Lifecycle Surfaces
options.body: Keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, and checkpoints as the supported compaction surfaces and document remaining needs as plugin or future design work.

recommendation.title: Warning And Checkpointed Handoff First
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in pre-threshold warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path while leaving agent-requested DEFER disabled until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal is the pre-compaction memoryFlush work, which is the closest existing handoff-like lifecycle behavior.
